notes: Both answers give PG's actual position: don't start a startup in college, waiting costs nothing, just learn, with the Facebook-style side-project exception. The deciding quotes I checked appear in the raw sources. A adds the test of whether the project is taking over your life, and B adds the 'build what you yourself want' point, so they come out about even.

Both answers get the core position right ('go, then come back', YC as the best way to do it, the unicorn stat) and quote the talk accurately. A wins narrowly because it also gives his second reason for discounting the stat: it measures valuation, not performance. Both miss his 'half as well is still good' point and his idea that Stockholm could become the Silicon Valley of Europe.

Both answers capture the key's position with the right specifics: leverage, 80–90% of deals chased, decksmithing, and the eight months at Justin.tv. I found the main quotes in the raw sources. A attributes each quote cleanly, and it credits the walk-away definition of leverage to Caldwell. B has broken citation fragments and preamble text, and it states the 'investors buying an option on you' point less precisely.

Both answers match the key and use the same quotes, which check out in the source. B adds clear source timestamps and a more useful legal caveat: his percentages are what he'd argue for, not what the cofounder is legally owed. A's caveat about vesting is slightly confused, and its sourcing notes are messy ("my sources rates").

Both answers correctly say the line was Altman's, not Tan's, quote the 'Gary probably can't' caveat, and explain the gap as compounding network effects that help founders find co-founders. A has broken leftovers (empty video and timestamp references, a stray vault path, 'my sources's'), and its claim that 'YC is the new Bay Area' is its own reading of the source. B is cleaner, with dated, verifiable citations.

Both answers reject the false premise and use quotes that check out in the sources. B is slightly better because its citations are clean and timestamped and it stays on Livingston. A has blank citation markers, and its Paul Graham 'formidable' aside is less relevant to the question.
